common_name: New Wonder Fan Flower (Compact Trailing Scaevola)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings after all frost danger has passed into well-drained soil or a container mix in full sun; New Wonder is a more compact, mounding selection than older lavender-blue scaevola cultivars and holds its shape well without becoming leggy.

directions: New Wonder is a naturally compact sport of the older Blue Wonder fan flower, forming a tighter mound of succulent, toothed foliage that still cascades gently over container rims rather than sprawling widely. Give it full sun and a well-drained mix, and let the soil surface dry slightly between waterings, since scaevola roots are prone to rot in soggy conditions. Its lavender-blue, one-sided fan flowers appear continuously from spring through frost without deadheading, and light shearing after a flush keeps the mound dense in Gulf Coast humidity. Because it is propagated only from cuttings, plants are purchased as started material rather than grown from seed.

common_name: Whirlwind Blue Fan Flower (Proven Winners Trailing Scaevola)

planting.note: Transplant after the last frost into a well-drained container mix or garden bed in full sun; Whirlwind Blue is a named color selection within the Proven Winners Whirlwind series bred for vigorous, uniform trailing habit and strong summer heat tolerance.

directions: Whirlwind Blue produces an especially heavy, uniform flush of true blue fan-shaped blossoms along long, trailing stems, making it a reliable single-color choice for hanging baskets and window boxes rather than the mixed-color effect of unnamed scaevola seedlings. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil and water when the top inch of the mix dries, since consistently soggy roots invite stem rot. It self-cleans without deadheading and tolerates Gulf Coast heat and humidity better than many older fan flower selections, though a mid-summer trim keeps the trailing stems from becoming sparse at the base. Feed lightly every few weeks through the growing season to sustain continuous bloom.

common_name: Outback Fan Dancer Fan Flower (Trailing Basket Scaevola)

planting.note: Plant out after the last frost in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained potting mix; Outback Fan Dancer is a vigorous trailing selection marketed for hanging baskets and mixed containers that holds continuous color through summer heat.

directions: Outback Fan Dancer sends out long, well-branched trailing stems studded with small, one-sided fan-shaped flowers, giving a fuller cascade than many older scaevola cultivars when grown in a hanging basket or tall container. It performs best in full sun but tolerates a few hours of afternoon shade in the hottest Gulf Coast summers without losing bloom density. Keep the potting mix evenly moist but never waterlogged, and pinch back any stray overly long runners in midsummer to keep the habit full rather than stringy. No deadheading is required, as spent flowers drop cleanly on their own.

common_name: Surdiva Purple Fan Flower (Heat-Tolerant Trailing Scaevola)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March-May. Surdiva Purple is a color selection within the Surdiva series bred for improved heat and humidity performance compared to older scaevola cultivars, making it a strong Gulf Coast basket choice.

directions: Surdiva Purple carries the same semi-trailing, self-branching habit as Surdiva Blue but in a deeper violet-purple flower color, giving basket and container plantings a richer contrast against silver or chartreuse companion foliage. It holds up through peak summer heat and humidity better than many older fan flower selections, continuing to bloom without deadheading from spring into fall. Grow it in full sun in well-drained soil, and avoid letting the root zone stay saturated, since scaevola is prone to root and stem rot in poorly drained containers. Light feeding every two to three weeks sustains the dense flower coverage typical of the Surdiva series.

common_name: Bombay Dark Blue Fan Flower (Compact Trailing Scaevola)

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost into well-drained soil or container mix in full sun; Bombay Dark Blue is a compact, well-branched selection within the Bombay series bred for uniform trailing habit and season-long color.

directions: Bombay Dark Blue forms a tidy, densely branched mound that trails moderately over container edges, producing masses of deep violet-blue fan-shaped flowers that stay in scale with smaller baskets and combination pots. Full sun and a well-drained mix keep the compact habit tight; the plant tolerates heat and short dry spells once established but performs best with even moisture. No deadheading is needed, as the small flowers drop cleanly after fading, and an occasional light pinch encourages fuller branching. Its restrained spread compared to more vigorous trailing scaevola series makes it useful where a smaller-scale filler or spiller is needed.

common_name: Scampi Blue Fan Flower (Cascading Container Scaevola)

planting.note: Transplant into well-drained soil or a container mix in full sun after the last frost; Scampi Blue is a fast-growing, sprawling selection within the Scampi series suited to hanging baskets, patio planters, and small-scale groundcover use.

directions: Scampi Blue grows quickly into a sprawling mound of green foliage covered in whorls of indigo-blue fan-shaped flowers that continue from mid-spring through summer without a break. It works equally well cascading from a hanging basket or spreading as a low, informal groundcover at the edge of a bed. Grow it in full sun with consistent moisture, letting the surface dry slightly between waterings to avoid root rot, and trim back leggy stems occasionally to keep new growth dense. Deadheading is not necessary, since the plant sheds spent blossoms on its own.
